comparison.current_label: v1.0 (after fixes informed by one held-out example)
comparison.caveat: This set is no longer fully unseen. The three v1.0 reading fixes (a company suffix marks an employer and a "Client:" line names a client; employment terms such as "Only W2" are not requirements; intro sentences such as "We are looking for a hands-on X to join our team" are context) were found by looking at one held-out example during a manual demo. They are general rules, tested with new examples, but the v1.0 column is not a blind result. The v0.4 and v0.5 columns are the blind results.

semantic.how_to_run: Install the ml extra (pip install -e ".[dev,ml]", with the CPU-only PyTorch first on Linux as the README shows), then run python -m evals.run --semantic. The first run downloads the two models from Hugging Face, about 180 MB.

llm.how_to_run: To run it with your own key, put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment or in a local .env file (see the README), then run python -m evals.run --llm. It makes one parse call per job and up to LLM_MAX_SUGGESTIONS rewrite candidates per pair (20 by default), billed to that key, and writes every candidate to llm_candidates.json next to this report.

error_analysis.title: Requirements that name no catalog skill are left for a person to check
error_analysis.observation: The rule parser only finds skills from the skill catalog. A requirement whose tools or domain are outside it gets no skills, and a degree or certification requirement the app can't judge is left to a person, so exact matching marks it needs_check whether the resume proves it, lacks it or shows it in part.

examples.what: "Knowledge of ISO ClaimSearch or other claims industry integrations": labeled direct; the parser found no catalog skill in it.
"Experience with causal inference methods such as propensity scores, difference-in-diffe...": labeled direct; the parser found no catalog skill in it.
"Salesforce Platform Developer II certification": labeled gap; the parser found no catalog skill in it.

error_analysis.title: Related experience needs matching by meaning
error_analysis.observation: In exact mode the app never returns adjacent, so related experience the labels mark adjacent (GitLab CI for GitHub Actions, Java for C#) comes out as gap, partial or needs_check. Matching by meaning is meant for these and wasn't run.

examples.what: "Experience with TeamCity or Jenkins build pipelines": labeled adjacent, app gap (Jenkins missing, CI/CD missing).
"Deep, hands-on experience running Amazon EKS in production": labeled adjacent, app gap (Amazon EKS missing).
"Experience building CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions or CircleCI": labeled adjacent, app gap (CI/CD missing, GitHub Actions missing).

error_analysis.title: Roles are found but the title or employer is split wrongly
error_analysis.observation: The role and its dates are read, but the title and employer are split in another place than the labels (extra text in one of them, or both in the title), so the role doesn't match its label.

examples.what: role 'Graduate Research Assistant, Example State University': Read as a role with title 'Graduate Research Assistant' and employer 'Example State University, Department of Statistics'. Extracted line: "Graduate Research Assistant – Example State University, Department of Statistics | Aug 2016 – Jun 2020".

role 'Adjunct Instructor, Sample Community College': Read as a role with title 'Adjunct Instructor, part-time' and employer 'Sample Community College'. Extracted line: "Sample Community College – Adjunct Instructor, part-time (01/2021 – 12/2021)".
education 'Master of Science, Information Systems': The degree or school was read differently. Extracted line: "Master of Science, Information Systems".

error_analysis.title: Company and posting details are kept as requirements
error_analysis.observation: Company descriptions and posting lines are kept as requirements, usually as context: they name a skill or address the candidate, so the parser can't tell them from a duty.

examples.what: "We are looking for a hands-on ClaimCenter developer to join the claims IT team." kept as context.
"Mock Payments, Inc. | Remote, US (Eastern or Central time zones preferred)" kept as preferred.
"The team supports 14 hospitals and more than 200 clinics with reporting on quality, finance and operations." kept as context.

error_analysis.title: A related skill or a missing detail is counted as direct proof
error_analysis.observation: The catalog files some tools under a broader skill as well (JUnit and NUnit also count as Unit testing, GitHub and GitLab as Git), so a requirement that names the broad skill can be proven by a line that names another tool, and a domain word ("payments") counts wherever a work line uses it.

examples.what: "Knowledge of PMD or other static code analysis tools for Apex": labeled partial, app direct from the experience line "Wrote Apex triggers on a trigger handler framework, plus batch and queueable Apex for n..." (Apex via 'Apex triggers').

"Experience building CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions or CircleCI": labeled adjacent, app direct from the experience line "Azure, AKS, AWS (EC2, S3), Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, Bicep, Helm, Kustomize, Flux,..." (CI/CD via 'GitLab CI').

"Experience implementing row-level security in Power BI.": labeled adjacent, app direct from the experience line "Built Power BI reports with DAX measures for the HR and procurement teams, published to..." (Power BI via 'Power BI').

error_analysis.title: Years requirements cite no resume lines
error_analysis.observation: For a years-only requirement the report gives the years it counted but no lines, while the labels cite the role header lines. These items always miss in evidence recall, which is why recall is also shown without them.

examples.what: "7+ years of overall IT experience": labeled direct; the report cites no lines (10.4 years read).
"7+ years of overall IT experience": labeled direct; the report cites no lines (7.4 years read).
"6+ years in infrastructure, DevOps, SRE or platform engineering roles": labeled direct; the report cites no lines (9.9 years read).

error_analysis.title: The status is right but the first lines cited aren't the labeled ones
error_analysis.observation: The status matches the label, but none of the report's first three lines is a labeled evidence line. Evidence is listed skill by skill, so the first lines can all come from one skill of the requirement, or from a broad skill such as ETL (matched by "data pipelines").

examples.what: "Experience with Salesforce integrations using REST and SOAP APIs": labeled direct, app direct; first line: certifications line "Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I" (Salesforce via 'Salesforce').

"At least 5 years of experience in business intelligence, data warehousing or reporting...": labeled direct, app direct; first line: experience line "Developed Informatica PowerCenter mappings that loaded the Oracle enterprise data wareh..." (Data warehousing via 'data warehouse').

"Experience with Salesforce DevOps tools such as Copado, Gearset or Salesforce DX": labeled direct, app direct; first line: certifications line "Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I" (Salesforce via 'Salesforce').

error_analysis.title: Labeled requirements are not extracted
error_analysis.observation: A labeled requirement line has no matching extracted requirement.

examples.what: "Experience: 5 - 8 Years" (required) not found.
"Educational Qualification: B.E./B.Tech/MCA or equivalent" (required) not found.

error_analysis.title: Work the labels count as shown is found only in a summary or skills line
error_analysis.observation: The labels count the work as shown in a bullet, but the bullet describes it in other words, so exact matching finds the skill only in the summary or skills section, or not at all, and calls the requirement partial.

examples.what: "4+ years of experience applying statistics or machine learning in industry": labeled direct, app partial (Statistics demonstrated, Machine learning listed).
"Solid understanding of dimensional modeling (star schemas, slowly changing dimensions).": labeled direct, app partial (Data modeling listed).

error_analysis.title: Labeled requirements missing from the report
error_analysis.observation: The job parser didn't extract the requirement, so the report has no status for it.

examples.what: "Experience: 5 - 8 Years": labeled direct; the parser didn't extract it.
"Educational Qualification: B.E./B.Tech/MCA or equivalent": labeled direct; the parser didn't extract it.

error_analysis.title: Date ranges with a separator the parser doesn't accept are not read
error_analysis.observation: The extracted header has a character between the two dates that the date pattern doesn't accept, so the role's months aren't counted.

examples.what: role 'Associate Salesforce Developer, Demo Technologies': No date range the app can read is on the line. Extracted line: "Associate Salesforce Developer | Demo Technologies, Chennai".

error_analysis.title: Required lines get the wrong priority
error_analysis.observation: A line gets another priority than its label: its section's priority, changed by wording in the line ("is a plus" makes it preferred, "you should" or "must" makes a context line required).

examples.what: "Take part in requirement discussions with onsite teams and client stakeholders." labeled context, parsed as required.

error_analysis.title: Years requirements fail when roles weren't read
error_analysis.observation: A years requirement is decided from the roles the app read: their total for "5+ years of experience", and the roles that mention the skill for "4+ years with Java". When a role is lost (see the structure patterns) the years fall short and the requirement becomes a gap or partial, or needs_check when no role was read at all.

examples.what: "5+ years of hands-on Salesforce development experience": labeled direct, app partial with 4.9 years read in roles that mention Salesforce.
